idiom_name: sql interpolator + Read/Write instances + ConnectionIO transact
implementation_notes: doobie is a pure-functional JDBC layer: the mapper is the Read[A]/Write[A] pair (derived for case classes, written by hand for awkward columns) and ConnectionIO composition is the unit of work - one transact(xa) runs a whole load-mutate-store sequence in a single transaction. Case classes stay plain data types with their own behaviour and no JDBC knowledge, while SQL lives in the mapper's methods. Prefer it when the codebase is already effect-based and you want transactions to be values rather than annotations.
pitfalls: Derived Read instances consume the selected columns in declaration order, so an added or reordered column shifts values whenever the JDBC types line up - keep the select list explicit and aligned with the case class.
Without transact the individual ConnectionIO values run in their own connections, so a load-modify-store sequence loses atomicity.
Read/Write instances for value objects, refined types and java.time values are where the mapper's real work lives; deriving them ad hoc at call sites scatters the mapping.
Write derivation for case classes with fields that have no database counterpart fails or persists unintended columns - mark such fields or map with an explicit Write.

variants.name: Slick lifted embedding with mapped projections
variants.idiom_name: Table subclass + <> projection mapping to a case class
variants.implementation_notes: Slick's lifted embedding is the mapper: a Table subclass declares columns and a * projection, and a bidirectional <> mapping (usually (User.tupled, User.unapply)) ties that projection to a case class, so queries are type-checked against the table definition. DBIO actions run through a Database, and transactionally groups them into one transaction. Choose it when you want a query DSL checked against the schema; accept that the table class is a second, parallel model of the case class that must be maintained next to it.
pitfalls: The * projection defines the mapping: reorder the columns in the table class and equal-typed fields map to the wrong case class fields without a compile error.
DBIO actions are lazy and run on the Database's execution context; a forgotten db.run or Futures mixed without transactionally splits the work across connections.
The table class duplicates the domain case class, so keep both in the mapper package and never let the domain file import Slick.
